article.story:
Portugal's new No. 7 Carlos Forbs gave the team its first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era with a 70th-minute goal in Tuesday's 3-2 win over Wales to clinch top spot in their UEFA Nations League group.

After a historic 4-1 home loss to Denmark on Saturday in their first match since Ronaldo's retirement from the national team, Portugal badly needed to bounce back in Cardiff against a Wales team already sure of finishing bottom of League A4.

And it was the man taking over Ronaldo's iconic jersey, which has been given a fresh look in honor of the country's record goalscorer, who ensured the win.

Just 11 minutes after coming on as a substitute, Club Brugge winger Forbs found the bottom corner of the net to clinch the comeback win that ensured Portugal moved into the quarterfinals as group winners ahead of second-placed Norway.

Despite an 11th-minute goal from captain Bruno Fernandes, Portugal had fallen behind to goals from Wales' David Brooks and Sorba Thomas.

But Pedro Neto equalized for the visitors late in the first half before Forbs' goal proved enough for the win despite Neto's 74th-minute sending off for a second yellow card.

The draw for the quarterfinals will take place on Friday, with the games to be held in March.

Wales, meanwhile, will go into the draw for the League A relegation/promotion playoff, which will also take place in March.

Poor defending and discipline were issues for Jorge Jesus' side, but there were still far more positives than on Saturday when Denmark inflicted Portugal's heaviest-ever competitive home loss. Portugal finished their Nations League group with five wins from six games in a campaign overshadowed by the absence of Ronaldo.

Tribute banners were again on show among the Portugal fans in Cardiff, nearly two months after Ronaldo's last game for Portugal, a 1-0 win over Wales in September.

Ronaldo fell out with coach Jesus when he was an unused substitute for the following game against Norway, and then walked out on the squad. He declared his retirement from the national team Nov. 5.

Fernandes gave Portugal the lead when he curled the ball into the top corner but it lasted just two minutes before Brooks leveled for Wales. When Thomas put Wales ahead on a rapid counter just before halftime, it was Portugal's turn for a quickfire equalizer from Neto.

Forbs scored the winner in the 70th with smart movement to set up a low shot.

It looked like Portugal might give the lead away again after Chelsea winger Neto was sent off for two reckless tackles in as many minutes, but Wales struggled to create many chances after that.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.
